rv.q: She is superbly duplicitous in the scene in which she appears to make amends to Jason even as she plans to kill his new wife.

For all its psychological astuteness, the production has one or two oddities. Tom Scutt's split-level set, with a Corinthian palace above and a dark forest below, seems too palpably symbolic of the play's division between public and private worlds.
Its textures are a mix of ancient and modern. Though it reverberates with a sense of Greek ritual, there's an acute feeling of up-to-dateness.
Despite its considerable theatrical merits I was, as ever, glad to escape 'Medea'.
I don't think I've ever been so traumatised by a theatrical production ever.

cn.t: Critics praise this visceral, psychologically astute production for its tragic force and contemporary resonance. Helen McCrory commands the stage in a traumatizing yet theatrically compelling take on Euripides' dark tale.
